text:
liz: Quick question on route precedence: if we have a host pattern `*.example.com` and a header-based service override `x-svc: payments`, which wins when both match? We hit it in prod with two routes.
omar: We currently match by most-specific host first, then header rules? I thought header overrides were higher priority.
jia: IIRC current matcher order is: exact host > host wildcard > path specificity > header match. Headers are tiebreakers only.
sam: That ordering caused the outage earlier — payments svc header was ignored because host matched a broad wildcard that had higher precedence. See <incident/4567|inc-4567>
liz: Example routes:
```yaml
- id: payments-vhost
  host: "payments.example.com"
  route_to: payments-service

- id: catchall
  host: "*.example.com"
  headers:
    x-svc: billing
  route_to: billing-service
```
jia: I'd like to propose two approaches: 1) Make header selectors higher priority than wildcard hosts. 2) Add explicit `priority` or `force_header_override` flag on a route so intent is explicit.
omar: Option 3: keep global precedence but add a router-level validation that warns when header+host overlap (fail the commit or require explicit opt-in).
route-bot: :warning: lint: found ambiguous overlap between `payments-vhost` and `catchall` — recommend adding `priority` or narrowing host pattern.
sam: For backward-compat, add explicit flag plus a config toggle to flip default behavior later. That minimizes surprises.
liz: Can someone file an RFC or open a tiny PR with tests? @omar @jia
